new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.weighted_bind
new_declarations.header:
private theorem weighted_bind (p : PMF α) (f : α → PMF β) (g : β → ℝ≥0∞) :
    (∑' b, p.bind f b * g b) = ∑' a, p a * (∑' b, f a b * g b)

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.weighted_pure
new_declarations.header:
private theorem weighted_pure (x : α) (g : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    (∑' a, PMF.pure x a * g a) = g x

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.weighted_map
new_declarations.header:
private theorem weighted_map (p : PMF α) (f : α → β) (g : β → ℝ≥0∞) :
    (∑' b, p.map f b * g b) = ∑' a, p a * g (f a)

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.weighted_add
new_declarations.header:
private theorem weighted_add (p : PMF α) (f g : α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    (∑' a, p a * (f a + g a)) = (∑' a, p a * f a) + ∑' a, p a * g a

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.weighted_const
new_declarations.header:
private theorem weighted_const (p : PMF α) (c : ℝ≥0∞) :
    (∑' a, p a * c) = c

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.workExpectation_mono
new_declarations.header:
theorem workExpectation_mono (k : Nat) (xs : List α) (f g : Outcome α → ℝ≥0∞)
    (h : ∀ result ∈ (run k xs).support, f result ≤ g result) :
    workExpectation k xs f ≤ workExpectation k xs g

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.workExpectation_const
new_declarations.header:
theorem workExpectation_const (k : Nat) (xs : List α) (c : ℝ≥0∞) :
    workExpectation k xs (fun _ => c) = c

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.workExpectation_add
new_declarations.header:
theorem workExpectation_add (k : Nat) (xs : List α) (f g : Outcome α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    workExpectation k xs (fun result => f result + g result) =
      workExpectation k xs f + workExpectation k xs g

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.workExpectation_mul
new_declarations.header:
theorem workExpectation_mul (k : Nat) (xs : List α) (c : ℝ≥0∞)
    (f : Outcome α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    workExpectation k xs (fun result => c * f result) = c * workExpectation k xs f

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.workExpectation_nil
new_declarations.header:
theorem workExpectation_nil (k : Nat) (f : Outcome α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    workExpectation k [] f = f (none, ([], 2))

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.workExpectation_cons
new_declarations.header:
theorem workExpectation_cons (k : Nat) (head : α) (tail : List α)
    (f : Outcome α → ℝ≥0∞) :
    workExpectation k (head :: tail) f =
      ∑ i : Fin (tail.length + 1),
        let action := stepRun k (head :: tail) i
        (((tail.length + 1 : Nat) : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹) *
          match action.1 with
          | Sum.inl (j, ys) => workExpectation j ys
              (fun result => f (prepend (head :: tail).length i.val action.2 result))
          | Sum.inr p => f (some p, ([((head :: tail).length, i.val)], action.2))

new_declarations.name: Resources.RandomSelection.scanExpectation_cons
new_declarations.header:
theorem scanExpectation_cons (k : Nat) (head : α) (tail : List α) :
    scanExpectation k (head :: tail) =
      ((tail.length + 1 : Nat) : ℝ≥0∞) +
        (((tail.length + 1 : Nat) : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹) *
          ∑ i : Fin (tail.length + 1),
            match (stepRun k (head :: tail) i).1 with
            | Sum.inl (j, ys) => scanExpectation j ys
            | Sum.inr _ => 0

new_declarations.name: Examples.RandomSelectionMean.selected_value_and_mean_bounds
new_declarations.header:
theorem selected_value_and_mean_bounds (k : Nat) (xs : List α) (hk : k < xs.length)
    (result : Outcome α) (hr : result ∈ (run k xs).support) :
    ∃ a, result.1 = some a ∧ Applications.Selection.RankedAt xs k a ∧
      (xs.length : ℝ) ≤ scanMean k xs ∧ scanMean k xs ≤ sourceMean k xs

prepared_type_scope: All 108 public declarations in the cumulative six-file assignment, with explicit @ and universes/explicit/full-name/proof printing. The 13 authored private helpers remain in source and mandatory exhaustive-audit scope.

statement_review.assessment: Weights are exactly the existing run PMF. General observations are nonnegative extended reals and may have infinite expectation. Laws use only PMF normalization, nonnegative summation and support inequalities. The conditional equation retains the exact measured step, actual selected child, recorded occurrence and direct return; it assumes no size independence or desired drift.

Definitions are standard lower integrals of the existing Nat marginal laws. Their weighted-run equations are proved by PMF map transport, preserving the coupling and unrestricted payload universe. No new probability law is assigned.

Existing actual pathwise finite support bounds prove lower-expectation finiteness and genuine real integrability. Natural division precedes the cast in the triangular bound. No linear expected bound, payload measurability, finite payload type or valid-rank premise is assumed.

The first full scan supplies the lower bound for all worker ranks. The same-run pathwise W<=T<=9W+2 supplies the affine mean bridge, including invalid empty-continuation cost 2. The scan equation pays active n and averages only the actual selected strict child, with zero scan continuation on equal-block termination.

These are actual real integrals on Nat. Separate finiteness theorems precede every finite-order transport from ENNReal, avoiding the toReal(infinity)=0 trap. Ranks remain zero-based worker ranks; no assertion about the public select rank-zero tariff is changed.

case_review.expected: Every worker rank on the empty list has means W=0,T=2, without an inhabited-payload premise.
For arbitrary x, valid singleton rank0 has means W=1,T=9.
Invalid worker rank1 on [7] has means W=1,T=11, retaining the empty continuation.
The actual two-key occurrence law has W=2 or3 and T=11 or20, each with weight1/2, giving real means5/2 and31/2. Both finite indices are exhausted.
For every x, the equal-value worker rank1 law has constant scan2 and indexed source costs12+i for i:Fin2, hence source mean25/2. No distinct-value resampling or Nodup assumption occurs.
The actual scan expectation equation on [0,1] is E[W]=2+(1/2)E[W on [0]], with only the actual pivot-one child.
For every ordered input type, list and worker rank, both actual scalar costs are integrable and their means compare via E[W]<=E[T]<=9E[W]+2.

For a valid rank and any supported outcome, its returned value is RankedAt, while the same-run expectations satisfy n<=E[W]<=E[T]. The theorem does not equate branch costs merely because all outputs agree.

architecture: Small local weighted-sum lemmas follow the already accepted RandomQuickSortMean proof pattern; only actual selection-run expectation laws are public. Standard Mathlib lower/real integrals are reused. No changes to accepted quicksort or prior checked selection modules.
